body:
When an original filing and its amendment share a filing date, `holdings_as_of` can choose the original solely because its database ID is larger. Rank visible filings by filed date, amendment status, then ID, matching the holdings-diff selector. Knowledge-time and supersession filters stay intact; schemas without a filing type retain the ID tie-break.

Closes #1668

## Tasks

- [x] Apply the filed-date, amendment-status, and ID authority policy in the production point-in-time selector.
- [x] Add a shared inverted-ID fixture with pre-amendment and exact knowledge-time cutoffs, exercised through tuple and mapping cursors.
- [x] Verify cross-selector agreement, normalized filing types, legacy schemas, equal-type ties, and filed-date precedence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `python -m pytest tests/test_bitemporal_holdings.py tests/test_diff_holdings.py`: 29 passed. AMENDED wins once known; ORIGINAL remains visible beforehand.
- [x] Restoring the ID-only tie comparison makes the named same-day knowledge-cutoff test fail; restoring the fix passes the full selector gate.

## Validation

Python 3.12.2. `python -m pytest tests/test_backtest_flow.py`: 14 passed. Focused Ruff, Black (target py312), mypy for `etl/point_in_time.py`, and `git diff --check` passed. SQLite tuple and mapping cursor paths were exercised; no live PostgreSQL run is claimed.

The new tests against the original production code failed in six cases, with 23 existing/control cases passing. Exact deliberate-break output is retained in a durable PR comment so automated body updates cannot erase it.
